title: Remove the fixed Personal Signal GPU overlay ceiling with geometric capacity growth

scope.subject: Dynamic Three.js point-buffer capacity for Personal Signal galaxy overlays

research_summary: The current Personal Signal Points geometry preallocates exactly 256 positions, creating a silent long-term ceiling as authored content grows. Three.js documents that BufferGeometry attributes cannot be efficiently resized in place once rendered; capacity overflow should be handled by allocating replacement geometry/attributes. Reuse that native BufferGeometry contract with power-of-two geometric growth, so normal updates reuse the existing typed buffer and only capacity-boundary crossings allocate a larger attribute.

sources.finding: Three.js BufferAttribute storage is backed by a fixed-length TypedArray; count derives from that array and content updates use needsUpdate/update ranges.
Three.js explicitly states rendered buffers cannot be resized in place; if growth exceeds preallocated capacity, create replacement geometry/buffers and release superseded GPU resources.
The Three.js manual notes TypedArrays require their size up front, so dynamic geometry requires explicit bookkeeping rather than array push semantics.

search_ladder.conclusion: The universe product and renderer backbone are already selected; this task only removes a capacity ceiling inside one existing Points overlay.
The existing React Three Fiber host already delegates GPU attribute storage to Three.js, so no new rendering framework is justified for a buffer-capacity concern.
No separate particle subsystem is needed because the existing Personal Signal overlay already uses one Three.js Points object and only its attribute capacity must grow.
Three.js BufferGeometry and BufferAttribute provide the exact replacement/update primitives; the only project-specific choice is when to allocate a larger typed buffer.

candidates.name: Three.js BufferAttribute replacement with power-of-two geometric growth
candidates.reason: Removes the hard ceiling while preserving the same Points/material path. Power-of-two growth amortizes reallocations so normal content updates only rewrite the existing typed array.

candidates.name: Reallocate the Three.js position buffer to exact signal count on every growth
candidates.reason: Removes the ceiling but causes unnecessary GPU/TypedArray churn when signals are added incrementally; geometric capacity preserves the same correctness with fewer reallocations.

candidates.name: Increase the fixed preallocated Personal Signal buffer
candidates.reason: A larger constant merely moves the hidden ceiling and wastes predictable GPU/CPU buffer memory for the common sparse-content case.

decision.rationale: Keep the existing Three.js Points overlay and reuse BufferAttribute replacement only when the required signal count exceeds capacity. Grow to a power-of-two bucket so sparse sites stay small, larger portfolios have no arbitrary ceiling, and incremental content additions do not repeatedly reallocate GPU buffers.
decision.fallback: If signal counts become large enough that a single Points draw itself is the bottleneck, retain this capacity contract while evaluating a dedicated instanced/clustered signal renderer as a separate subsystem task.
